review.verdict: F1 and F2 lens: both findings are FIXED in v0.2 within the producer's declared local trust model (same OS account, private state root). No P0 (no route to launch a transport, write a repository, or renew consumed authority through the controls) and no P1 (both fixes are real and the core regressions have specific, code-asserting tests). Two P2 gaps must close before a synthetic live pilot: (1) the operator-facing CLI permit/dispatch path (bridge.mjs:62-72), including the attempt-root containment and recipe-reconstruction guard, has zero test coverage, so a regression there is caught only post-consumption by runRecipe (burning the authorization and holding the slot); (2) consumption tombstones live beside transport.json, and stateId is only a field in transport.json, so a transport.json copied or restored alone into another directory silently resurrects an unconsumed permit for the same signed envelope; REVIEW_FIXES.md:11 overstates this as impossible. Remaining items are P3 (canonical-JSON interop spec for the external coordinator, trust pin only inside transport.json, Windows-only guards untested and the whole guard unproven on Windows, minor state-machine/doc precision, reproduction-tool wording). Evidence integrity: both packages match their own MANIFEST.json byte-for-byte (v0.1 27/27, v0.2 75/75), so all citations are against shipped bytes and the v0.1 folder is unmodified. Recommendation for this lens: ACCEPT WITH LIMITS for F1/F2, conditional on the two P2 items and a native Windows run before any synthetic pilot.

findings.claim: Consumption tombstones are stored beside transport.json and stateId is only a field inside transport.json, so a transport.json copied or restored alone into a different directory (or with authorization-use/ removed) silently resurrects the unconsumed permit for the same signed envelope; REVIEW_FIXES.md:11 overstates this as impossible for a new state directory.
findings.evidence: core.mjs:19 blankState generates stateId and it is persisted only in transport.json; :44-48 integrity-checks events and job digests but not stateId/permits/authorizations; :148 markerPath = <store.dir>/authorization-use/<key>.json, a sibling of transport.json; grantPermit :178-181 returns the existing permit whenever the ledger copy has consumedAt===null and no marker exists; consume :202 checks only markers in the current directory. Audience binding :159 blocks only a FRESHLY provisioned store (test tests/core.test.mjs:46 uses a new random stateId); test :44 covers rollback in the SAME directory where markers survive. A pre-consumption transport.json placed in an empty directory therefore passes read() (:35-49) with the same stateId and no markers. docs/REVIEW_FIXES.md:11 states 'An envelope cannot be reused by creating a new state directory'; the hedge in the same paragraph covers only 'replace the pinned key, entire state and use markers', not copying transport.json alone. This is an operator backup/restore mistake, not only a hostile act.
findings.fix: Code (cheap partial hardening): at provisioning write an O_EXCL store-id marker (e.g. <store.dir>/authorization-use/.store-<stateId>) and in Store.read() refuse a transport.json whose stateId has no matching marker in that directory (STATE_MARKERS_MISSING), and refuse when the marker directory is absent but permits/authorizations are non-empty. Docs: reword REVIEW_FIXES.md:11 to 'cannot be reused in a freshly provisioned store (different stateId); the state directory including authorization-use/ is the unit of backup and restore, never transport.json alone', add the same rule to LIVE_PILOT.md:16, and keep the statement that only the coordinator ledger prevents cross-store reissue.

findings.claim: The canonical JSON the external coordinator must sign is under-specified relative to what primitives.mjs implements, so a non-Node issuer can produce signatures that fail closed and block the pilot.
findings.evidence: docs/AUTHORIZATION_CONTRACT.md:8 specifies only sorted keys, array order and no whitespace. primitives.mjs:6-10 additionally implies JSON.stringify number formatting (1 vs 1.0, 1e+21), JSON.stringify string escaping, and key ordering by JavaScript default sort (UTF-16 code units). Verification at core.mjs:158 uses canonical(parsed body), so any divergence yields BAD_SIGNATURE (safe) but non-interoperable. No published test vector exists in the package.
findings.fix: Pin the canonical form explicitly (reference RFC 8785 JCS, or state: ASCII keys only, integers only, no floats, strings without control characters) and ship one test vector: a sample body, its exact canonical bytes, and a signature under a published synthetic test public key, plus a test in tests/core.test.mjs that verifies that fixed vector.

findings.claim: The pinned coordinator public key lives only inside transport.json and is re-validated for shape but not identity on read, so a transport.json replacement with a different key is accepted; a sibling O_EXCL trust pin would make this detectable at low cost.
findings.evidence: core.mjs:27 enforces TRUST_ALREADY_PINNED only through initialize(); read() :39 calls normalizeTrust(s.coordinatorTrust) which checks shape and key type only; no independent file records the trust fingerprint, unlike consumption markers (:148,:209). Acknowledged as out of the local trust model at docs/REVIEW_FIXES.md:11 and docs/SECURITY_AND_LIMITS.md:18.
findings.fix: At initialize({trust}) write <store.dir>/authorization-use/.trust-<hash(normalized)> with writeNew (O_EXCL) and in read() require that exactly that marker exists for s.coordinatorTrust (TRUST_PIN_MISMATCH otherwise). Keep the documented caveat that a same-account writer can still remove both.

P3 (operational, Windows pilot): consume writes tombstones (core.mjs:209) before mutate's atomicJSON rewrite (core.mjs:59 -> paths.mjs:103 renameSync). If the rename fails (Windows antivirus/indexer holding transport.json open, ENOSPC), the markers remain while transport.json still shows the permit unconsumed; the next dispatch is refused at core.mjs:202 AUTHORIZATION_CONSUMED and the signed decision is burned with no attempt made. Correct per the fail-closed design, but LIVE_PILOT.md should warn that a transient state-write failure costs a new coordinator decision.

P3 (hygiene): the attempt root is <store>/attempts (core.mjs:237; bridge.mjs:60,67), so the only process the bridge launches runs with cwd two levels below transport.json and authorization-use/. Within the declared same-account trust model this is acceptable, but a sibling root (e.g. <store>-attempts) would keep the authority ledger out of the provider child's working tree at zero cost; docs/SECURITY_AND_LIMITS.md:21 already admits the bridge is not the provider's sandbox.

P3 (hardening): the evidence recordRef is not tombstoned (core.mjs:141-147 keys only {issuer,evidence.sha256}); a re-signed envelope with the same recordRef and a new sha256 is accepted as fresh evidence, which only the coordinator currently prevents (AUTHORIZATION_CONTRACT.md:36,40 are accurate about this). A fourth key hash({issuer,recordRef}) would close same-reference renewal locally.

P3 (operator footgun): core.mjs:15 crypto.createPublicKey(trust.publicKeyPem) also accepts a PRIVATE key PEM and derives the public key, so `init --trust` with a pasted private key succeeds silently (only the SPKI is stored at :17). Refuse PEMs containing 'PRIVATE KEY' before pinning.

P3 (robustness): primitives.mjs:15 validId accepts prototype property names ('constructor', 'toString', 'hasOwnProperty', 'valueOf'); an authorizationId of 'constructor' makes core.mjs:178 find Object.prototype.constructor as `old` and :180 hash(old.envelope) throws a TypeError (hash(undefined) -> createHash().update(undefined)) instead of a BridgeError; enqueue with such a job id fails with JOB_CONFLICT (core.mjs:98). All fail closed, but use Object.hasOwn/null-prototype maps or exclude those names from validId.

Upheld only in narrowed form; part of the evidence is FALSE. Verified true: core.mjs:273 sets RECONCILED_UNKNOWN, :274 returns nextAttemptNeedsNewAuthorization:true, grantPermit :185 and consume :204 accept only PREPARED/RESOURCE_BLOCKED/FAILED/OUTPUT_REJECTED, so that JOB ID is terminal; tests/core.test.mjs:71 proves only AUTHORIZATION_CONSUMED for the same envelope. FALSE: 'enqueue :99-100 dedups by digest so a new job ID with identical content returns the reconciled job' and 'a fresh spec digest/store is required'. enqueue hashes the whole spec at core.mjs:95 (hash(spec) via canonical(), and spec.id is a required field per :85), and read() :42 enforces job.spec.id===id && hash(job.spec)===job.digest, so changing only the id changes the digest and creates a new PREPARED job; the :99-100 duplicate branch can only match a job already found by s.jobs[spec.id] at :97 and is effectively unreachable. Consequently the same content IS re-attemptable under a new job ID with a new signed authorization (authorizationScope :136-139 binds jobId/jobDigest, so a new authorization is needed anyway), and no new store is required. The surviving P3 is doc/return-field precision: :274 and docs/LIVE_PILOT.md:41 should say 'new job ID plus new authorization', and LIVE_PILOT.md:39 ('do not retry via a new ID') is an operator rule the code does not enforce. missed: CORRECTION to lens F-004 / F3 residual (2) / F4 residual (7) / F4 docsOverstate: the claim that RECONCILED_UNKNOWN makes 'that spec digest' permanently un-retryable and that 'a new spec digest or store is required' is false. lib/core.mjs:95 digest=hash(spec) canonicalises the whole spec including the required id (:85), and read() :42 enforces hash(job.spec)===job.digest, so re-enqueueing identical content under a new job ID produces a new digest and a fresh PREPARED job; the :99-100 duplicate branch is effectively unreachable (it can only match what :97 already found). Only the job ID is terminal; a new ID plus a new signed authorization (scope binds jobId/jobDigest, :136-139) suffices. docs/LIVE_PILOT.md:39 'do not retry via a new ID' is an unenforced operator rule.

MISSED P3 (defense in depth, operator-error-gated): dispatch's post-runner state writes never re-check slot ownership. lib/core.mjs:245, :249, :253, :258 and :261 mutate s.jobs[id] and (at :249/:258/:261) set s.active=null without asserting s.active?.job===id or that s.active.request.attemptId equals this attempt. acknowledgeStopped :272 deliberately accepts status DISPATCHING. If an operator runs `recover` against a still-live controller (contrary to LIVE_PILOT.md:41) and then dispatches job B, the late-returning dispatch for job A overwrites RECONCILED_UNKNOWN and clears s.active while B's process is running, so a third consume (:195) would succeed. Precondition is operator misuse, so P3; fix: in each late mutation require s.active?.job===id && s.active.request?.attemptId===request.attemptId, otherwise record a LATE_RETURN event and leave active/status untouched.

MISSED P3 (receipt accuracy, ordering NOT PROVEN read-only): lib/providers.mjs:163 child.stdin.end(Buffer,()=>{if(!receipt.stdinError)receipt.inputSent=true;}) ignores the callback's error argument. In Node >=15 Writable.end() callbacks are invoked with an error on destroy (errorBuffer runs on nextTick before emitErrorCloseNT), so after an EPIPE the callback can run before the 'error' listener at :161 sets stdinError, recording inputSent:true for a write that failed. No safety impact: stop('STDIN_ERROR') still fires -> UNKNOWN held; and at :185 inputSent only gates COMPLETED. Fix: check the callback's err argument.

MISSED P3 (operability, NOT PROVEN for the installed CLIs): a provider that exits before draining stdin (bad flag, auth failure) with a prompt larger than the pipe buffer causes EPIPE -> lib/providers.mjs:161 stop('STDIN_ERROR') -> UNKNOWN held, or if close wins the race, empty stdout -> MISSING_COMPLETION/INVALID_PROVIDER_JSON -> :191 UNKNOWN held. v0.1 :73 deliberately ignored EPIPE. So most fast provider failures will need `recover` and a new job ID rather than landing FAILED. Safe direction; document in LIVE_PILOT.md so the operator expects it.

PRECISION on lens F-001 residual: on Windows an externally killed child (code 1, signal null, partial non-JSON stdout) lands UNKNOWN via INVALID_PROVIDER_JSON for Claude (decode at :54) or MISSING_COMPLETION for Codex with empty stdout (:71), not uniformly 'via MISSING_COMPLETION'; both reach :191 UNKNOWN and core.mjs:252/:243 hold the slot.
